passage: On Friday Wasim told his teacher that his maths sheet was at home, though he had left it on the bus. Nobody knew, yet a small stone sat in his stomach all day. That afternoon there was a quiz, and when the teacher stepped out, the answer key lay open on the desk. His heart pounded. He had promised himself that morning not to look, so he stood up, went to the window and counted the pigeons on the wall until the teacher came back. After school he told the teacher the truth about the sheet, and the teacher nodded and thanked him. That evening his parents, Gopika and Mridul, went to a wedding and left him alone at home for the first time, with the rules: door locked, no stove, homework done. The sweet tin sat open on the shelf, nobody was watching, and the chore list said sweep the balcony. Wasim took exactly one sweet, swept the balcony, finished his homework and texted, "All done, home safe," at nine. When his parents returned, Mridul checked the balcony and smiled. Gopika said next time he could stay a bit longer, and Wasim felt very grown up.

qa.q: What did Wasim count while the teacher was out of the room?
qa.a: He counted the pigeons on the wall.

qa.q: How did Wasim's plan about the answer key differ from the way the small lie about his maths sheet weighed on him?
qa.a: For the answer key he decided in the morning not to look and simply walked to the window, but the lie about the sheet had already been told, so it sat like a small stone in his stomach until he told the teacher the truth.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when the answer key lay open on the desk?
qa.a: His heart pounded, so he felt tempted and nervous.

qa.q: What can Wasim expect from keeping his parents' trust while nobody is watching?
qa.a: He can expect more freedom, as Gopika showed by saying he could stay a bit longer next time. 🙂

grounding: One child faces a small lie nobody knows about, an open answer key, an unwatched sweet tin and parents' trust when left alone, and keeps his integrity.
